text:
J.T. Compher has five goals in 18 games, four of them in his last ten, and two in Detroit's last two wins. Prashanth Iyer of Expected By Whom called Friday's 2-0 win in Columbus "easily J.T. Compher's best game of the season." On a Red Wings team that lost seven of eight in the middle of November, his goals have stood out.

They won't keep coming at this rate. He's shooting 20% against 12% last season, with five goals on 2.48 expected, and our talent range puts his finishing closer to 13%. His chance rate (0.54 expected goals per 60) is almost identical to last year's.

The bigger concern is his line's five-on-five share. Detroit has only 42.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his relative number is more than seven points below his teammates. Evolving-Hockey rated him 264th among 401 forwards last season, with most of his value from even-strength offense and penalties drawn. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries. A Stanley Cup winner with Colorado in 2022, he's a useful middle-six piece. Watch whether the chance share improves before the shooting cools.
